q: The crust of the Earth is composed predominantly of:
explanation: The crust is made up mainly of igneous rocks, with sedimentary and metamorphic rocks derived from them; granite and basalt are the commonest crustal rocks.

q: The breakdown of rocks at the Earth's surface by physical, chemical and biological agents is called:
explanation: Weathering is the in-situ breakdown of rocks at or near the surface; erosion is the removal and transport of the weathered material by agents such as water, wind and ice.

q: Metamorphic rocks are formed from:
options: molten magma that cools below the Earth's surface
sedimentary deposits compacted by the weight of overlying rocks
volcanic ejecta deposited on the sea floor
existing rocks altered by heat and pressure
explanation: Metamorphic rocks such as marble, slate and gneiss are formed when pre-existing igneous or sedimentary rocks are recrystallised under great heat and pressure within the crust.

q: According to W.M. Davis, the stage of the erosional cycle of a river marked by the greatest stream power and maximum relief is the:
explanation: Davis' cycle passes through youth, maturity and old age; in the mature stage the river has cut a deep valley with the maximum relief, after which the landscape is graded in the old age stage.

q: A horst and a graben are landforms produced by:
explanation: A horst is an uplifted block and a graben a depressed block between parallel faults; the Narmada and Tapi valleys are classic graben examples in India.

q: In geology, an unconformity indicates:
options: a gap in the geological record caused by a period of erosion or non-deposition
an igneous intrusion into older rock
explanation: An unconformity is a surface of erosion or non-deposition separating two rock sequences of different ages, and it is important in relative age determination.

q: The term 'batholith' refers to:
options: a narrow ridge of folded sedimentary rock
a deep-seated, irregular mass of igneous rock
a dome-shaped volcanic cone built of ash and cinders
a sheet of lava that has intruded between rock layers
explanation: A batholith is a very large, irregular body of intrusive igneous rock with no clear margins, while a laccolith is a dome-shaped intrusion within sedimentary rock.

q: The Mercalli scale measures:
options: the energy released by an earthquake
the intensity of an earthquake at a particular place
explanation: The Mercalli scale describes the observed effects of an earthquake at a place, while the Richter scale and the moment magnitude scale measure the energy released.

q: The State Disaster Management Authority in a State is chaired by the:
explanation: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 the State Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the Chief Minister, while the District Authority is chaired by the District Collector.

q: The District Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the:
options: Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad
explanation: Section 11 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 provides that the District Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the District Collector or the District Magistrate.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction?
options: Investing in disaster risk resilience for development
Promoting the use of nuclear energy in disaster response
explanation: The four Sendai priorities are understanding disaster risk, strengthening governance, investing in resilience and preparedness with effective response and building back better.

q: The National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) was financed by the:
explanation: The NCRMP, which built coastal shelters, cyclone warning systems and coastal embankments, was financed by the World Bank and implemented with state governments.

q: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre is located at:
explanation: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre set up by the National Disaster Management Authority with INCOIS support is located at Hyderabad.

q: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the National Executive Committee is chaired by the:
explanation: The National Executive Committee, which prepares the national disaster management plan and monitors implementation, is chaired by the Prime Minister.

q: The 1999 Odisha Super Cyclone caused comparatively few deaths mainly because:
options: the cyclone struck only at low tide
the state had built cyclone shelters and evacuated people on a massive scale
the army restored the coastline before the surge arrived
explanation: About two million people were evacuated to cyclone shelters before the October 1999 super cyclone hit Odisha, which is why the death toll stayed far below the estimated figure.

q: The National Earthquake Management Organisation, the nodal agency for seismic hazards, is under the:
explanation: NEMO operates the National Seismic Monitoring Network and is an autonomous body under the Department of Earth Sciences in the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

q: Mica is used principally in the manufacture of:
explanation: Because of its excellent dielectric properties, mica is used in electrical insulation, capacitors and electronic components; it is also used in cosmetics and paints.

q: The Mumbai High oil field was discovered in:
explanation: The Mumbai High field in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Maharashtra was discovered in 1974 and remains the largest onshore-offshore oil field of India.

q: The Digboi oil field in Assam is notable because it is:
options: the oldest oil field in India
the largest oil field in India
the only offshore oil field in India
the first field to produce natural gas
explanation: The Digboi field in upper Assam, discovered in 1889, is the oldest oil field in India and the first one where crude oil was found in the country.

q: The monazite sands of the Kerala coast are an important source of:
explanation: Monazite beach sands along the Kerala coast carry thorium, which is why India has one of the world's largest thorium reserves and can pursue thorium-based nuclear fuel cycles.

q: India's largest reserves of thorium are found in the monazite sands of:
explanation: The monazite beach sands of the Thiruvananthapuram district, particularly Manavalakkurathil, hold India's largest thorium reserves, followed by the sands of Odisha and Tamil Nadu.

q: The Khetri copper mines are located in:
explanation: The Khetri and Zawar belt in Rajasthan is the principal copper producing belt of India, with the Khetri copper mines dating back to the colonial period.

q: The Singhbhum mineral belt is particularly rich in:
explanation: The Singhbhum belt of Jharkhand and Odisha is the classic mineral heartland of India, famous for iron ore, copper, mica and uranium deposits.

q: The trade winds blow:
options: from the equatorial low towards the poles
from the subtropical high pressure belt towards the equatorial low pressure belt
from west to east along the equator
from the polar high towards the equator
explanation: The trade winds blow from the subtropical high pressure belts towards the equatorial low pressure belt, deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

q: The 'Roaring Forties', 'Furious Fifties' and 'Screaming Sixties' denote:
options: the trade winds of the Pacific
the strong westerly winds of the Southern Ocean
the monsoon winds of the Indian Ocean
explanation: These are the names for the persistent strong westerly winds of the Southern Ocean, which are unobstructed by land and were used by early sailing ships to reach Australia and the Americas.

q: The Koppen classification of the world's climate is based mainly on:
explanation: Koppen's scheme classifies climate using mean monthly temperature and precipitation thresholds, which is why it is the most widely used world climate classification.

q: The Thornthwaite classification of climate is based on:
options: the average length of the dry season only
the ratio of potential evapotranspiration to precipitation
explanation: Thornthwaite's method uses the water balance, comparing potential evapotranspiration with precipitation, which is why his classification is also called the moisture index classification.

q: The albedo of a surface is:
options: the total radiation absorbed by the atmosphere
the ratio of reflected to incident solar radiation
the ratio of outgoing long-wave radiation to incoming short-wave radiation
explanation: Albedo is the reflecting power of a surface expressed as the ratio of reflected to incident radiation; fresh snow has a high albedo while forest and dark ocean surfaces have a low one.

q: The Hadley cell of atmospheric circulation extends:
options: vertically from the surface to the stratosphere
from the equator to about 30 degrees latitude in each hemisphere
from the poles to 60 degrees latitude
explanation: The Hadley cell is the low latitude circulation cell in which air rises at the equator and descends near 30 degrees latitude, producing the subtropical high pressure belts and the trade winds.

q: The Walker Circulation in the Pacific Ocean is a component of:
explanation: The Walker Circulation is the east-west overturning cell in the equatorial Pacific, and its weakening or reversal during an El Nino event is the core of the ENSO system.

q: The 'Horn of Africa' comprises mainly:
explanation: The Horn of Africa projects into the Indian Ocean and comprises Ethiopia, Eritrea, Somalia and Djibouti, the region that guards the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

q: The Serengeti plains are located mainly in:
explanation: The Serengeti ecosystem lies in northern Tanzania and adjoining Kenya and is famous for the annual wildebeest migration and the Maasai Mara game reserve.

q: The Cape Fold Mountains of South Africa are especially noted for:
options: rich deposits of gold, diamonds and other minerals
the largest expanse of tropical rainforest
the greatest concentration of volcanoes in Africa
the highest waterfalls on the continent
explanation: The old folded mountains of the Cape region hold the diamond belt of Kimberley and the gold reefs of the Witwatersrand, which shaped the country's mining economy.

q: The Great Artesian Basin, the largest artesian basin in the world, is located in:
explanation: The Great Artesian Basin underlies about one-fifth of Australia and yields the deep artesian bores that supply water to the dry interior and the artesian spa towns of the region.

q: Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, lies between:
explanation: Titicaca straddles the Peru-Bolivia border at about 3,800 metres, drains into the Lake Poopó and supports the reed boat tradition of the Uros islands.

q: The Irrawaddy river flows through which country?
explanation: The Irrawaddy flows through Myanmar and forms the axis of the country's rice-growing delta before reaching the Andaman Sea.

q: The Mozambique Channel separates:
options: Sri Lanka from the Indian mainland
explanation: The Mozambique Channel lies between Madagascar and the African mainland, roughly 400 kilometres wide at its narrowest, and is rich in marine life.

q: The Palghat Gap lies between the:
options: Palni Hills and the Cardamom Hills
Anamalai Hills and the Western Ghats
Nilgiri Hills and the Javadi Hills
Nilgiri Hills and the Anaimalai Hills
explanation: The Palghat or Palakkad Gap, about 15 kilometres wide, separates the Nilgiri Hills from the Anaimalai Hills and lets the south-west monsoon winds pass into the interior of the peninsula.

q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are separated from the mainland of India by the:
explanation: The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman group from the Nicobar group, while the Coco Channel separates the Nicobars from the Indonesian island of Sumatra.

q: Barren Island, in the Andaman group, is notable as:
options: the site of India's first rocket launching station
the only active volcano in India
the largest coral island of the Indian Ocean
explanation: Barren Island, about 135 kilometres north-east of Port Blair, hosts India's only active volcano, whose eruptions have continued intermittently.

q: The Bhabar and the Terai belts along the southern Himalayan foothills are formed by:
options: alluvium carried down by the Himalayan rivers
marine deposits of the Cretaceous period
black soil deposited by the Deccan rivers
explanation: As Himalayan rivers descend they deposit coarse boulders and sand in the Bhabar belt and finer, fertile alluvium in the Terai, and the belt is marked by disappearing streams.

q: The Khasi and Jaintia hills with the Shillong Plateau form part of which physiographic division of India?
explanation: The North-Eastern Hills, also called the Purvanchal, include the Patkai, Naga, Manipur and Mizo hills along with the Shillong Plateau, and are separated from the Himalayan ranges by the Bengal gap.

q: The Panchmarhi hills form the highest point of the:
explanation: Panchmarhi at 1,050 metres is the highest point of the Satpura range, whose Maikal spur forms the northern edge of the Deccan Plateau.

q: The physiographic division of India that is bounded on the west by the Arabian Sea and on the east by the Bay of Bengal is the:
explanation: The Peninsular Plateau is the broad tableland flanked by the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats, with the Arabian Sea to the west and the Bay of Bengal to the east.

q: The abyssal plain of the ocean floor lies at a depth of about:
explanation: Below the continental slope lies the abyssal plain, the flattest and largest area of the ocean floor at depths of roughly 4,000 to 6,000 metres, covered by fine ooze.

q: The Atlantic Ocean has a higher average salinity than the Pacific Ocean mainly because it has:
options: a much larger inflow of river water
greater precipitation over the ocean surface
explanation: Salinity is controlled by evaporation and precipitation; the Atlantic loses more water by evaporation than it gains, and its narrower basin allows less freshening from river discharge, so it averages about 35 parts per thousand.

q: The Mediterranean Sea is remarkable because it is:
options: a deep ocean basin of the Pacific
almost landlocked, with exchange restricted to the Strait of Gibraltar
a marginal sea of the Atlantic with free exchange of water
a part of the Indian Ocean
explanation: The Mediterranean is a semi-enclosed sea with a narrow outlet at Gibraltar, so intense evaporation makes its salinity very high, well above the average of the open ocean.

q: Spring tides occur during the:
explanation: When the sun, moon and earth are in a straight line, as at the new and full moon, the solar and lunar tidal forces reinforce each other and produce spring tides of greatest range.

q: The thermohaline circulation of the ocean is also known as:
options: the monsoon drift of the Indian Ocean
explanation: Differences in temperature and salinity drive a slow global overturning of deep water from the North Atlantic towards the Pacific, the great ocean conveyor belt that also stores carbon in the deep ocean.

q: The Caspian Sea is notable because it is:
options: a large lagoon of the Pacific
a landlocked salt lake, the largest enclosed inland body of water
a deep sea connected to the Atlantic Ocean
a fjord of the Arctic Ocean
explanation: The Caspian Sea is the largest enclosed inland body of water, a saline lake fed by the Volga, the Ural and the Kura rivers, and its shores are shared by five countries.
